description: Conformance manifest (ST-5.4, AD-19). Every shipped studio skill MUST have an entry here — the runner discovers surfaces from the plugin's skills/ tree and fails any surface missing from this manifest (and any manifest entry with no shipped skill behind it). Drives run the surface's deterministic core headless in a throwaway sandbox project with an isolated store: stdin closed, wall-clock bounded, output must be machine-readable. argv[0] is plugin-root-relative; {sandbox} substitutes the sandbox project directory.

expect_semantics.json: process completes within the timeout and stdout parses as JSON
expect_semantics.ok: process completes within the timeout, stdout parses as JSON, AND the parsed object carries ok=true — the drive's internal assertions all held (e2e drives whose value is the chain succeeding, not merely answering)
expect_semantics.refusal: process completes within the timeout and refuses cleanly — nonzero exit, JSON with ok=false, or an in-band structured block proven by the declared marker (detect's ask, orchestrate's needs-onboarding) — and when a marker is declared the refusal MUST name it in stdout: an unnamed refusal (a crash, an unrelated error) gives the skill layer nothing to surface as blocked (ISS-002); never a prompt, never a hang

tk-studio-activate.auth_preflight: none needed — read-only local four-plane check; harness auth is the driver's preflight (driver-contract §1)

tk-studio-install.auth_preflight: npm registry only (npx at the bmad.lock pin) — no Anthropic auth in the surface itself; installer verifies the manifest against the pin after install

tk-studio-base-update.auth_preflight: npm registry (installer rerun at the new pin) + VCS remote for the integration PR; both verified by failing loud, never hanging

tk-studio-detect.auth_preflight: none needed — pure read of the project tree

tk-studio-onboard.auth_preflight: none needed — local standup + propose/record; vault linking skips cleanly when unconfigured

tk-studio-orchestrator.auth_preflight: none needed — stateless read of store + project config

tk-studio-plan-sync.auth_preflight: local backends need none; the jira binding (AD-7) runs the API-token preflight before any backend call — GET /myself proves the token AND the org-admin toggle in one probe, then the issue-type scheme is confirmed against the AD-6 default mapping; unconfigured/unauthenticated runs block named, never a silent 401 (the sandbox drive below proves the block without any network)

tk-studio-job.auth_preflight: none needed — local run-state reads/writes and substrate directives only; when a run invokes a target skill, that skill's own preflight posture applies (one surface, one preflight)

drives.note: the ST-9.4 e2e drive — the run the source lifecycle never had: run-init -> seed -> boundary handoff with deltas -> the wrapper's finish -> queue materialized (deduped on the knowledge.schema.json key) -> routing doc rendered -> the promotion gate opens (ST-9.5: check + dry-run draft walk clean); every step asserted, expect ok means the chain succeeded, not merely answered
the capture verb refuses an unknown run named — never a guess, never a silently empty queue

tk-studio-session.auth_preflight: none needed — local run-workspace reads/writes only; delta validation is pure (lib/knowledge.py)

drives.note: mints the resumable run the boundary drives below split (drives share the sandbox/store and run in order); the timestamped run id is why the session drives select via --job-id

tk-studio-knowledge.auth_preflight: VCS remote + gh only at the push/PR step, both failing loud (a push failure lands the draft commit locally and says so; a gh failure reports the branch as pushed with manual-PR guidance); emit's fetch is best-effort (offline answers from last-fetched refs) — the routing-doc gate, queue read, promoted-baseline dedupe, emission baseline, and sanitization scan are local and need no auth

drives.note: the ST-9.5 refusal drive — a promotion attempt without a rendered routing doc refuses named (the routing doc is the human's promotion-decision surface; D3): a promotion drafted from data no human has seen is not a gated promotion

the ST-9.6 emission verb (D4) — reconciles the promotions record against merged promotion PRs, exactly once per PR; a sandbox with no recorded drafts answers a clean no-op before any git read, never an error

tk-studio-observe.auth_preflight: none needed — local ledger append only

tk-studio-research.auth_preflight: none needed in the deterministic core — charter validation and workspace writes are local; the researching agent's web access rides the harness's own auth (driver-contract §1 preflight)

drives.note: the ST-9.3 seed surface: an invalid artifact refuses named before any run or store read (a knowledge.schema.json-shaped seed against a real run is exercised by the lib suite; intrinsic invalidity is the driver-visible posture)

tk-studio-measure-push.auth_preflight: VCS remote + gh only at the push/PR step, both failing loud (a push failure lands the branch commit locally and says so; a gh failure reports the branch as pushed with manual-PR guidance) — the sanitization re-check and unpushed computation are local and need no auth

tk-studio-consolidate.auth_preflight: none needed — reads the merged measurements/ files and writes issues/ledger.md locally; no network, no backend

tk-studio-migrate.auth_preflight: the import step runs the jira adapter's API-token preflight (token + org-admin toggle + issue-type scheme) before any backend write; inventory, verification bookkeeping, and the cutover flag are local — an unconfigured/empty project blocks named before any network (the drives below prove it)

tk-studio-report.auth_preflight: none needed — local ledger append only
